title: The diameter is set by the largest required area, not by the stage with the lowest flooding velocity
purpose: Proposal 0015, Part I, section 2: each stage's required vapour-flow area is A_j = Vdot_j / (f u_fl,j), and the diameter is set by the largest A_j. Here the top stage has the lowest flooding velocity (the densest vapour) but carries less vapour than the bottom stage (the vapour flow below a subcooled feed is larger, slide 35 of Fermeglia 2021), so the bottom stage sets the diameter. A rule "the stage with the lowest flooding velocity sets the diameter" (slide 35, which holds when every stage carries the same vapour flow) would give a column too narrow for its bottom section.

source.citation: M. Fermeglia, Staged column design, University of Trieste (2021), slides 35-38 and 44 (the method); the stage values are this case's own, chosen so that the ranking holds for any fitted form of Fair's chart

units: SI: m3/s, kg/m3, mN/m (= dyn/cm), mass-flow ratio

design.why_the_ranking_does_not_depend_on_the_c: the three stages have the same flow parameter F_lv = (W_L/W_V)(rho_V/rho_L)^0.5 = 0.1 and the same surface tension, so C_sb(F_lv, spacing) is the same on every stage and cancels from the ratios of the flooding velocities and of the required areas, whatever fitted form of Fair's chart is used

behaviour: the lowest flooding velocity is on stage 2 (fixture: u_fl over C_sb per stage)
the largest required area, and so the diameter, is on stage 15; the diameter is that of A_15, larger than stage 2's by the ratio in the fixture (sqrt(A_15 / A_2) = 1.212)
the result names stage 15 as the stage that sets the diameter and reports every stage's fraction of flooding at that diameter

tolerances.why: the ratios are exact (C_sb cancels); only rounding remains
